Whether M should include the 'All prior years' aggregate (movement about -45.9m incurred by residual, a large share) is a scope question for the author: M over the printed years is +17.88m. 1729_2023.basis: Gross of reinsurance ('Estimate of cumulative gross claims incurred ... Less cumulative gross paid'), underwriting-year basis. Ties: liabilities sum to 368,826 as printed; est-paid=liability holds column by column (e.g. 2021: 180,537-122,790 = 57,747; 2022: 207,436-97,433 = 110,003). The 2022 table total 284,789 also sums.
1729_2023.note: The 2023 table ties to the 2023 accounts (implied gross incurred 192.8m against 193.6m, -0.4%), so M within it stands (+16.77m USD, 2021 column contributes only -0.4m). The cross-report differences are the stated GBP-to-USD presentation change (factor 1.2037 on every cell) except the 2021 column's end-2022 estimate, which is 58.3m USD above the converted 2022 print. The evidence says the 2022 print is the faulty one: its implied 2022 incurred is 120.7m GBP against 166.0m in its own accounts (-27.3%), and it would tie (about 169.2m, +1.9%) if the 2021 one-year-later cell were 150.3m GBP (180,947/1.2037) instead of 101.9m; the 2022 print's liabilities still sum to its balance sheet, so estimate and paid of that column were evidently both low. That bears on 1729/2022 (its M used the faulty cell), not on this record. The cross-table paid test (+34%) is distorted by the same 2021 column (cross-table paid on it +87.2m USD).
